requirements.text: Enqueued jobs are persisted and survive process restarts
Failed jobs are retried with backoff up to a limit, then moved to a dead state for inspection or replay
A job is held by one worker at a time; a crashed worker's job is re-claimed after its lease expires
Handlers get a stable idempotency key so at-least-once execution does not repeat external effects
Job payloads are validated before the handler runs
Worker concurrency is bounded and shutdown waits for in-flight jobs
Failures, queue depth, job age and dead jobs are visible to operators

evidence.name: failed jobs respect retry availability and become dead at the attempt ceiling
claims are distinct and stale owners cannot complete or extend a replaced lease
claims are distinct and stale owners cannot complete or extend a replaced lease

implementations.notes: PostgreSQL inbox (PostgresWebhookInbox) on in-process PGlite: delayed retry availability, attempt ceiling and dead state; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim with lease expiry, re-claim and stale-owner rejection; the same idempotency key across re-claims. The retry delay is fixed per call (not exponential), dead-job replay is not tested, and honoring the key at the external provider is the application's work. The pg-boss runner path is not exercised

pg-boss runner: payload parsing before the handler, worker concurrency limits and graceful stop are not exercised (the pack test only checks the runner refuses work before start); durable-enqueue is left here because the PGlite test recreates the adapter over the same in-memory database rather than restarting a process

evidence.name: outbox commits state and messages atomically and relays at least once
idempotency store runs once, replays, and reports conflicts

implementations.notes: In-memory store; a shared store is the application's work
